module.purpose: Implements the interactive node and selection dragging lifecycle for an XY graph, including snapping, constrained positioning, auto-pan, callbacks, and cleanup.
module.summary: This module binds d3-drag to a graph container and coordinates pointer events with graph state. It selects draggable nodes, tracks drag thresholds and multitouch cancellation, calculates snapped and extent-constrained positions, updates internal node coordinates, auto-pans near container edges, and invokes node, selection, and generic drag callbacks at start, movement, and completion.
module.businessContext: Supports graph-editor node manipulation and selection movement. Failure would prevent users from repositioning nodes, moving selections, snapping layouts, or receiving drag lifecycle notifications.
functions: XYDrag (~L102-418): Creates and manages graph node and selection dragging behavior
update (~L122-408): Binds d3-drag behavior and configures draggable container interactions
updateNodes (~L131-230): Calculates constrained positions and publishes changed node coordinates
autoPan (~L232-256): Repeatedly pans the graph while dragging near container boundaries
startDrag (~L258-300): Initializes dragged items and emits drag-start callbacks
destroy (~L410-412): Removes the installed d3 drag event handlers

mutationOfArg: Mutates each dragged item's position and internals.positionAbsolute during movement.

preconditions: The supplied getStoreItems function returns the store state and operations required by the drag lifecycle.
update must be called with a DOM node before drag events can be handled.
Drag event targets must satisfy the configured button, no-drag-class, and handle-selector filters to begin a drag.
postconditions: The returned instance exposes update and destroy operations.
A completed drag commits changed node positions and invokes applicable drag-stop callbacks.
Destroy removes the installed .drag behavior from the currently selected DOM node.
invariants: Node positions are updated only when the computed position differs from the current position.
Node positions are constrained through calculateNodePosition and optionally snapped to the configured grid.
A drag involving multiple nodes preserves the multi-node drag and snapping behavior as a group.
Drag lifecycle callbacks receive the current dragged node or selection and the current dragged-node collection.
Multi-touch continuation and dragging a node that has been deleted are aborted without continuing position updates.
edgeCases: When nodeDragThreshold is zero, dragging starts on the initial drag-start event; otherwise movement must exceed the threshold before drag items are initialized.
A touchmove event with more than one touch aborts the drag; if items were already collected, their positions are sent to updateNodePositions with the non-final flag.
If the dragged node is removed from nodeLookup during dragging, further drag updates are aborted.
If no nodes are draggable or selected for the drag, position and lifecycle callbacks that require drag items are not invoked.
If auto-pan is disabled while an auto-pan loop is active, the animation frame is cancelled and auto-pan state is reset.
If a drag produces no position change, updateNodePositions and movement callbacks are not invoked for that movement.
If the container has no bounding rectangle, auto-pan performs no movement.
If a node in the active drag collection is deleted, it is skipped during position calculation.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: Invalid drag targets are rejected by the configured event filter. Aborted or threshold-incomplete drags return without applying drag updates; no explicit exception or fallback error is produced.

detail.summary: Creates a drag controller that binds node and selection drag behavior to a DOM element through its update method and removes that behavior through destroy. Dragging updates node positions, supports selection, snapping, thresholds, auto-pan, and drag lifecycle callbacks.

Node positions are committed only when at least one dragged node position changes, and the final drag state is committed on drag end.
invariants: Nodes absent from nodeLookup are skipped during position updates.
Position-change notifications are not emitted when calculated positions equal the existing positions.
When snapToGrid is enabled, calculated positions are snapped using the configured snap grid.
Dragging is filtered by the primary-button condition, no-drag class, and optional handle selector.
A drag is aborted for multi-touch touchmove events or when the dragged node is deleted during the drag.

When the drag threshold is nonzero, dragging does not start until client-coordinate movement is greater than nodeDragThreshold.

When auto-pan is disabled, any active auto-pan animation is cancelled and auto-pan state is reset.
When the container bounds are unavailable, auto-pan performs no work.
When a multi-node drag uses an extent and grid snapping, a shared snap offset and adjusted extent are used to preserve group movement constraints.
